newsitem.title: UK: Freeze, ice blockages boost NWE gas oil premiums.
newsitem.headline: Freeze, ice blockages boost NWE gas oil premiums.

text.p: Rising heating oil demand and ice-blocked German waterways boosted NWE gas oil premiums as Europe shivered in freezing temperatures on Monday, traders said.
"German demand is enormous. Ice (in some of the waterways) is affecting the market there," one trader said.

Heating oil barge premiums rose 50 cents to trade at Jan IPE +$1.50 on delivery delays caused by the iced-up German barge channels with further rises expected if forecasted cold weather continues and wholesalers need to replenish storage.
Most German heating oil is moving on road and rail in view of the barge delays.
"My feeling is 0.2 is going to strengthen later in the week on the cold weather. But low sulphur is dead," a trader said.
Low sulphur diesel was steady at Jan IPE +$11/12.
Benchmark Jan IPE futures closed 75 cents up at $223.50 a tonne buoyed by the cold weather across Europe.

Heating oil cargo premiums rose 50 cents to $1 to Jan IPE +$5.50/6.50 on increased demand. A cargo of 880 gravity heating oil traded at cif high NWE -$0.25 into Lorient, at least $1 firmer. Low sulphur diesel was quiet at around Jan IPE +$9/10.
Arbs to Asia and the Untied States have closed.
